analyst.summary: HDB Financial is a diversified HDFC-Bank-backed NBFC (Asset Finance/Enterprise Lending/Consumer Finance, ~38/38/24 split, 74% secured) that went through a genuine FY25-26 asset-quality stress episode in unsecured business loans and the used-CV/construction-equipment book (Gross Stage 3 peaking ~2.81% in Sep-2025) and has been visibly healing since (down to ~2.3-2.4% by Q1 FY27, net slippages moderating, credit cost tracking toward management's 2.3% steady-state target, PCR ~56%). The single biggest overhang from the IPO era -- RBI's draft rule that could have forced HDFC Bank to cut its stake below 20% on business-overlap grounds -- was dropped in the October-2025 final guidelines, removing that specific tail risk. Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026) delivered a genuinely strong pre-provision quarter (NII +20% YoY, NIM 8.4%, PPOP +25%) though the headline ~38% PAT growth is partly a low-base effect against a stress-depressed year-ago quarter. Set against this: AUM/loan growth (~11% YoY) has run persistently below management's own 18-20% medium-term guidance, ROE (~14-15%) trails Bajaj Finance/Cholamandalam (~19%+) by a wide margin while the stock's ~3.0x P/B is not obviously cheaper than Shriram Finance's ~1.9x for comparable-or-better returns and growth, and a real supply-overhang date sits on the calendar (16.67cr HDFC-Bank-held shares off lock-in 2-Jan-2027). Net: hold the existing position -- the healing asset quality and resolved regulatory overhang argue against selling a clean, adequately-capitalised subsidiary of India's largest private bank, but the unproven growth reacceleration and peer-relative valuation gap argue equally against adding.
